# Causeline

> Causeline is an open-source (Apache 2.0), local-first debugging tool for React and Spring Boot apps. It traces one user action from a React click, through Spring Boot controllers, services, repositories, SQL and outbound calls, and back to the React state update, and shows it as one timeline. It names the bottleneck, flags OWASP Top 10 security hints on captured traffic, replays and compares requests, shows which span grows under load, and follows Spring AI and Python (FastAPI, LangChain) model and RAG calls in the same trace. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot can read the same traces and replay allowlisted requests over MCP (Model Context Protocol). It runs inside the developer's Spring Boot app at `/causeline`, for development and QA only, never in production.

Current version: `0.1.0-alpha.5` (alpha, released 2026-11-02). Requirements: Java 21+, Spring Boot 4.1 on Spring MVC or WebFlux, React 18 or 19 (or Next.js on the Node.js runtime). The optional Python library needs Python 3.10+ and Causeline 0.1.0-alpha.5 or later.

Key facts:

- No account, APM agent, collector or extra process. Traces live in memory inside the app (latest 1,000 traces, within 64 MB).
- Off by default (`causeline.enabled=false`) and refuses to start under a `prod*` or `production` profile.
- Built on standards: W3C `traceparent`, Micrometer Observation and OpenTelemetry. Can export redacted spans over OTLP to Jaeger, Grafana Tempo or an OpenTelemetry Collector.
- Captures headers, cookies, request and response bodies, SQL with bound values, method arguments and return values, and exceptions, and shows them in the local UI. Anything can be blocked with `causeline.capture.*`. Everything that leaves the app (OTLP, trace files, bug reports, forwarding, persistence) is redacted by default.
- Overhead measured on the demo: about 2 ms added at p99 for a full checkout with everything captured. The React SDK is under 10 KB gzipped and does nothing in production builds.
- Coverage: Spring MVC and WebFlux, JDBC and R2DBC, `RestClient`/`WebClient` calls, Kafka and RabbitMQ message spans, `@Async`, multiple Spring Boot services (`causeline.export.upstream`), React (fetch, XHR, state, Redux, renders), Next.js server code, Spring AI 2.0 model calls and vector searches, and FastAPI with LangChain.

Install:

- Maven: `dev.causeline:causeline-spring-boot:0.1.0-alpha.5`, then `causeline.enabled: true` in a dev profile. The app log prints a `Causeline UI:` link with an access token.
- npm: `npm install @causeline/react@alpha`, wrap the app in `<CauselineProvider endpoint="/causeline/api/spans">`, and wrap a click handler in `trace('Checkout', async () => { ... })`.
- Optional: `@causeline/next` for Next.js server spans, `dev.causeline:causeline-test` (test scope) for JUnit 5 trace assertions, and `pip install "causeline[langchain]"` for a FastAPI service that your Spring app calls (`causeline.init(endpoint="http://localhost:8080", service="ai-service")`, then `causeline.instrument(app)`; the token is read from `CAUSELINE_TOKEN`).
- With Spring Security, permit `/causeline/**`; Causeline protects those paths with its own access token.
- MCP (optional): the app log prints a `Causeline MCP:` command. For Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http causeline http://localhost:8080/causeline/mcp --header "X-Causeline-Token: <token>"`. Cursor, VS Code and other clients use the same URL and header; Claude Desktop connects through `npx mcp-remote`.

## Features

- Timeline: one trace from the React click to the state update, with HTTP requests, controllers, `@Observed` services, repositories, transactions, SQL, outbound calls, messages, logs and renders, ordered by the span tree
- Diagnosis: bottleneck by self time, N+1 query hints with fixes (JOIN FETCH, `@EntityGraph`, batch fetching), long-transaction hints, Explain query for captured SQL, exceptions with the file and line that threw (including caught-and-logged ones), open in editor, Check contract against the app's OpenAPI document
- Replay: resend a captured request to local, dev or QA; edit the path, query, headers or body first; pause at controller or service methods and change their arguments like a debugger; compare any two traces span by span, including response-body diff
- Security hints (OWASP Top 10:2025): read-only checks on captured traffic, such as a secret in a log, URL or response, a request value built into SQL or steering an outbound call (SSRF), insecure cookies and response headers, permissive CORS and stack traces in responses; a cross-trace security overview with dismiss
- Active probes: one hand-sent request each, from the replay form: another ID (IDOR), extra field (mass assignment), redirect elsewhere (open redirect), without a header (auth boundary); verdicts read from the replay's own trace. Not a scanner and never automatic; complements ZAP or Burp
- Load replay: send a captured request or a whole flow many times (fixed in flight, ramp, or rate), with p50/p95/p99, statuses and exceptions, and "what grew": which span's self time grew under load. Copy as k6 to run real load elsewhere. Goes only to local or to targets with `allow-load: true`
- Spring AI and RAG: with Spring AI 2.0, model calls and vector searches join the timeline with no setup, streaming included. The RAG panel shows the query, ranked chunks with scores, the final prompt with each chunk marked In prompt or Not in prompt, the answer and its tokens. Plain rules (no model) flag an empty retrieval, low relevance, duplicate chunks, a chunk that missed the prompt, an answer cut off by its token limit and a context near its limit. Prompts, answers and documents are withheld from exports and from coding agents; a replay, load run or agent replay that would call a model again is refused until `causeline.load.allow-ai` or `causeline.mcp.replay.allow-ai` is set. Comparing two runs shows chunks added, removed and moved, and score and token changes
- Python library (`causeline` on PyPI): FastAPI and LangChain spans join the Spring app’s trace and appear in the same RAG panel. Spans go to the Causeline inside the Spring app and need its access token. Off by default and in production; prompts and answers go only to a Causeline on the same machine unless `send_ai_text=True`
- Copy as: cURL, HTTPie, fetch, k6, and MockMvc or WebTestClient tests with trace assertions filled in
- JUnit guard (`causeline-test`): `@CauselineTest`, `RecordedTraces`, `TraceAssert` with `hasNoFailedSpans()`, `hasException(...)`, `hasQueryCountAtMost(n)`, `hasNoRepeatedQueries()`, `hasSpans(...)`, `hasNoSecurityFindings()`; never timing assertions
- Sharing: redacted trace export and import, and an HTML bug report
- Coding agents over MCP: `/causeline/mcp` lets Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or Claude Desktop list traces, read a trace with its insights and security hints, compare runs, find source files and replay a request. Everything the agent sees is redacted like an export; it replays only GET and HEAD, or what `causeline.mcp.replay.allow` lists, and only to local or `allow-mcp` targets. Connect with `claude mcp add --transport http causeline http://localhost:8080/causeline/mcp --header "X-Causeline-Token: <token>"`

## Packages

- [causeline-spring-boot on Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/dev.causeline/causeline-spring-boot): the Spring Boot starter, with the UI bundled
- [causeline-test on Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/dev.causeline/causeline-test): JUnit 5 trace assertions
- [@causeline/react on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@causeline/react): browser SDK (`CauselineProvider`, `trace`, `useTracedCallback`, `useTracedState`, `causelineReduxMiddleware`, `CauselineProfiler`)
- [@causeline/next on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@causeline/next): Next.js server tracing (`registerCauseline`, `createCauselineSpanProcessor`, `propagateFetch`)
- [causeline on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/causeline/): FastAPI and LangChain tracing for the RAG panel (`init`, `instrument`, optional `scored_retriever` and `traced_embeddings`)

## Optional

- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/causeline/causeline): issues and pull requests welcome; report security problems privately via Security → Report a vulnerability
- [Demo apps](https://github.com/causeline/causeline/tree/main/examples): Spring MVC checkout, WebFlux checkout, React page, Next.js page and a FastAPI and LangChain assistant, with slow, failing, contended and deliberately insecure scenarios
